project.name: PersonaRAG
project.description: An evidence-grounded conversational AI that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation to simulate the publicly documented perspectives of public figures, answering in their voice with inline citations. It includes a Python RAG pipeline (hybrid BM25 + embedding retrieval with ChromaDB), a FastAPI backend, and a React web frontend.

nodes.name: api.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI backend exposing persona listing, config, source browsing, and chat/panel endpoints, including NDJSON streaming variants consumed by the React frontend.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses StreamingResponse with generator functions emitting newline-delimited JSON, and a ThreadPoolExecutor with as_completed to stream panel answers as they finish.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit UI offering a single-persona chat tab with grounding badges and cited sources, plus a multi-persona panel tab with moderator summary.
nodes.languageNotes: st.cache_resource caches the PersonaEngine across Streamlit reruns.

nodes.name: run_eval.py
nodes.summary: CLI evaluation harness that scores retrieval quality (hit rate, MRR) per persona from a YAML question set, optionally comparing retrieval modes, generating answers, scoring grounding/abstention, and running LLM-as-judge faithfulness.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for personarag declaring its docstring and __version__.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Core persona engine orchestrating retrieve, prompt, generate, and grounding score, defining the Answer result type and the citation-coverage grounding report.

nodes.name: llm.py
nodes.summary: LLM backend abstraction with a streaming Protocol, Anthropic Claude and local Ollama implementations, a complete() helper, and a provider factory.
nodes.languageNotes: typing.Protocol gives structural typing so any object with name and stream() qualifies as an LLM.

nodes.name: panel.py
nodes.summary: Panel mode: runs several personas on the same question in parallel threads and asks a moderator LLM to compare their answers.

nodes.name: personas.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Persona data model and loads/lists persona definitions from per-persona directories.

nodes.name: prompts.py
nodes.summary: Prompt templates: answer modes, persona system prompt, numbered source formatting for [n] citations, user turn construction, and moderator prompts for panels.

nodes.name: retrieval_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes hit and reciprocal-rank metrics for retrieved hits against an eval item's expected sources.

nodes.name: judge

nodes.name: compare_modes

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what PersonaRAG does: it simulates public figures' documented perspectives by answering only from evidence in per-persona knowledge bases built from blogs, YouTube talks and podcasts. The README outlines the architecture, the web and Streamlit quick starts, and how videos and podcasts become searchable knowledge, giving you the map for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Settings and Environment
tour.description: config.py is the most depended-upon module in the project: it loads .env and exposes paths, embedding and re-ranking model names, chunk sizes, retrieval mode and similarity thresholds. env.template shows which knobs a user sets, such as choosing Claude or a local Ollama model, while requirements.txt lists the stack (ChromaDB, sentence-transformers, BM25, FastAPI, Streamlit, faster-whisper). Understanding these settings first makes every later component easier to read.

tour.title: Personas as Data
tour.description: Each persona is defined by data rather than code: persona.yaml describes background, expertise, communication style and known positions, while sources.yaml lists the blogs, talks and podcasts that form its knowledge base. personas.py turns these directories into Persona objects, and it is the second most widely imported module. Adding a new figure is therefore mostly a matter of adding YAML files.
tour.languageLesson: YAML manifests separate content from code: the Python loader maps keys into a typed data model, so new personas can be added without touching source files.

tour.title: Ingesting Sources
tour.description: Before a persona can answer anything, its sources must be turned into text. loaders.py converts local files, web pages, YouTube captions and podcast audio into plain-text Documents with metadata, relying on transcribe.py, which downloads audio with yt-dlp and transcribes it with a lazily loaded Whisper model. ingest.py is the CLI that drives this pipeline for a persona and reports counts and errors.

tour.title: Chunking and Snapshots
tour.description: chunking.py splits each document into overlapping word-window chunks along sentence boundaries, carrying source metadata forward so every chunk can later be cited. snapshot.py exports a knowledge base to portable JSONL (text and metadata, no vectors) and restores it, so the index can be rebuilt without re-fetching or re-transcribing sources.

tour.title: Hybrid Retrieval Store
tour.description: store.py is the retrieval heart of the system, built on the chunks from Step 5. It stores embeddings in ChromaDB, maintains a BM25 keyword index, merges both rankings with reciprocal rank fusion, and re-ranks the candidate pool with a cross-encoder. Combining lexical and semantic search catches both exact names and paraphrased ideas, which matters when evidence must be precise.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal rank fusion scores each document as the sum of 1/(k + rank) across rankers, so results that rank well in several lists rise to the top without needing comparable raw scores.

tour.title: Prompts and LLM Backends
tour.description: prompts.py formats the retrieved passages as numbered sources so the model can cite them inline as [n], and builds the persona system prompt, answer modes and moderator prompts. llm.py hides the model provider behind a streaming Protocol with Anthropic Claude and local Ollama implementations plus a factory, which is how the provider choice from Step 2 takes effect.
tour.languageLesson: Python's typing.Protocol enables structural typing: any class with matching method signatures satisfies the interface without inheriting from it, keeping LLM backends loosely coupled.

tour.title: The Grounded Answer Engine
tour.description: engine.py ties the previous steps together: retrieve from the store, build the prompt, generate with the LLM, then score grounding. It defines the Answer result type and the citation-coverage grounding report behind the strong, partial, weak and ungrounded labels shown in the UIs. panel.py builds on the engine by running several personas on the same question in parallel threads and asking a moderator LLM to compare their answers.

tour.title: FastAPI and Streamlit Entry Points
tour.description: Two front doors expose the engine. api.py is the primary runtime: a FastAPI server with persona, config, source and chat/panel endpoints, including NDJSON streaming variants, and it also serves the built React app. app.py is a Streamlit alternative with a chat tab showing grounding badges and cited sources plus a panel tab with a moderator summary; its config.toml disables the file watcher to avoid optional-import errors.
tour.languageLesson: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) streams one JSON object per line, letting clients parse tokens and metadata incrementally over a single HTTP response without WebSockets.

tour.title: Frontend Bootstrap and API Client
tour.description: The React client starts at main.tsx, which mounts App.tsx; App loads personas, modes and config from the backend and persists preferences in localStorage. api.ts is the typed client shared by every view, defining persona, source and grounding types and reading the NDJSON stream from Step 9 with an async generator. The frontend README and vite.config.ts explain the dev workflow and the /api proxy to the FastAPI server on port 8000.
tour.languageLesson: An async generator (async function*) lets TypeScript code consume a streamed response with for await...of, yielding each parsed NDJSON line as it arrives.

tour.title: Chat and Panel Views
tour.description: Chat.tsx streams a single persona's answer token by token with abort support, and Panel.tsx streams several personas plus the moderator summary introduced in Step 8. Answer.tsx renders markdown safely and turns [n] markers into clickable citation buttons, flagging invalid ones, while GroundingBadge.tsx and SourcesDrawer.tsx surface the grounding report and the retrieved evidence behind each answer.

tour.title: Evaluation and Tests
tour.description: Quality is measured, not assumed. run_eval.py scores retrieval per persona with hit rate and MRR using YAML question sets that list expected source IDs, keywords and unanswerable questions, and it can compare retrieval modes. test_core.py unit-tests pieces covered earlier: chunking, subtitle parsing, BM25 tokenization, RRF fusion and the grounding report citation logic.
tour.languageLesson: Mean Reciprocal Rank averages 1/rank of the first relevant result across queries, rewarding retrievers that put the right evidence at the very top.
